answer_text:
Interpreting \(W\) as the subspace generated by the powers of \(A\),

\[
W=\operatorname{span}\{A^m:m\ge 0\},
\]

we have

\[
\dim W^\circ = \dim M_n(\mathbb R)-\dim W = n^2-\dim W.
\]

The dimension of \(W\) is the degree of the minimal polynomial of \(A\). Since \(A^0=I\in W\), we always have \(\dim W\ge 1\). This minimum is attained, for example, when \(A\) is a scalar matrix (such as \(A=0\) or \(A=I\)), in which case \(W=\operatorname{span}\{I\}\) has dimension \(1\).

Therefore the maximum possible dimension of the annihilator is

\[
\boxed{n^2-1}.
\]

If a numerical integer is required, \(n\) must be specified; for a fixed \(n\), the integer is \(n^2-1\).
